session_title: The meticulous planning of the "beginner's game"
theme: 娱乐-新奇体验/策略筹备

content.text: Xingchen, I saw the script genre table you posted yesterday, and I’m quite interested in the immersive script that focuses on breaking alibis and the emotional one that supposedly has a group decision-making session at the end. However, as beginners, if we jump right in, would we end up "suffering" or ruin the experience for others? Should we first form a "newbie-friendly group with friends and family"? Just like the first time we teamed up to play games, starting with familiar faces might be better.

Wow, Xiaomeng, your 'project-based' thinking is really impressive! No wonder you come from a user operations background—you’ve thought this through so thoroughly. I completely agree that organizing our own carpool is much more relaxed, and we can even bring friends along to join the fun. This reminds me of how we planned the offline networking event for our 'boss'—we also started with our circle of acquaintances to ensure a harmonious atmosphere.

Thanks for the compliment! Just like when we planned the pet social before, I think preparing in advance can make everyone have more fun. After all, I’m a bit of a "worrywart," you know. So, I’ll dive into researching some "beginner-friendly" scripts and pick a few options, just like how I studied game hero rankings and designed event posters back then.

No problem! I'm in charge of recruiting people. I have a friend who's a logic whiz but has never played before—I think he'd be perfect for that script about cracking an alibi. Also, I can ask that DM who's really patient with new players and see if we can book him. I'm pretty good at gathering people, from forming gaming teams to promoting pet events—my social skills are always on point, haha!

Alright, clear division of tasks! I've done some research and picked out two options. Let me send this one to you first. This "Whale Circus" looks quite dreamy, with moderate difficulty, making it suitable for beginners. The packaging design reminds me of the aesthetic game skins you shared before, like the one with the long green hair.

Got it! Wow, this packaging design is really interesting. The combination of blue and pink reminds me of the aesthetic style of the game skins I shared before. Your taste in scripts is getting better and better—from losing streaks in games to the progress you’ve made now, you’ve grown so quickly! I still remember how frustrated you looked when you first shared your game stats screenshot, and now you’ve become a skilled planner.

Haha, thanks for the encouragement. Another alternative is "Farewell Poem," an emotional script. The writing is said to be very delicate, and it ends with a collective decision, which should spark a lot of discussion. This kind of focus on emotional experience feels a bit like setting up the "Most Adorable Contrast Award" during our pet activities—both are meant to promote interaction and resonance.

This emotional script looks quite heartfelt, with a blue and white background and text designed to evoke strong feelings. It reminds me of when we set up the "Most Adorable Contrast Award" during our pet event, which also focused on emotional experiences. Let me create a simple comparison table to help everyone make a choice. I’m familiar with making tables, just like the game hero rankings and script genre table I shared with you last time.

Great! You were very organized when you created the game hero rankings before, so this table will definitely be a big help. Just like how we planned the pet social event schedule, let's consider all the details.

Yeah, here's a look at the table I made. "Whale Circus" focuses on deduction and mechanics, with a lighthearted emotional tone, while "Farewell Poem" places more emphasis on the emotional storyline, featuring delicate writing. Both are marked for their newbie-friendliness. Does the style of this table remind you a bit of the script type table I shared earlier? Aiming for clarity and practicality.

The table is very clear! Just like we previously discussed the segmentation of pet fan communities, the information is presented at a glance. I think both notebooks have their own unique features, so we could let everyone vote to choose. However, I suggest adding the duration and number of participants, which would make it easier for everyone to plan their time.

Added. Sending it out like this should help everyone make a quick decision. By the way, I’ve already reached out to that logic-obsessed friend and the patient DM, and they’ve both expressed interest. Looks like my invitation skills are still as sharp as ever—from games to script murder mysteries, I never miss!

You're so efficient! It seems your social skills are always on point, from gaming livestreams to those sociable moments with your pet 'boss'. Let's discuss the time slots next. Weekends might work best for everyone, just like when we set up pet playdates—let's pick a time that works for everyone.

Exactly, either weekend afternoon or evening works. We can first gather everyone's opinions, just like making collective decisions in a script murder game—democratic decision-making! I suggest next Saturday afternoon, lasting 3–4 hours. What do you think? This schedule reminds me of our last gaming session, which was also arranged for the weekend—we had a great time without disrupting other plans.

Next Saturday afternoon sounds good, plenty of time. Let me organize the information: the script options are "The Whale Circus" and "Farewell Poem," with potential participants including you, me, our logical friend, and that DM. The time slot is tentatively set for next Saturday afternoon. It feels like we've completed another small event planning session—from games to pets, and now to script murder mysteries. Our coordination is getting better and better.

Perfect summary! This 'newbie round' was meticulously planned, from your proposal to the division of tasks and execution—everything flowed seamlessly. It feels like we’re not just gaming partners and event planning collaborators anymore; we’ve leveled up to become an entertainment exploration squad, with fun as the top priority! Just as I said before, let’s reject boredom and live in the moment. This scripted murder mystery is definitely going to be a blast!

Yes, the feeling of growing together is wonderful. So let's settle it like this for now—the script options, the list of participants, and the time slots are all set. Next, we'll wait for everyone's feedback before finalizing everything. Looking forward to our first script murder experience! I hope it becomes another wonderful memory, just like our first game victory or the success of 'Boss's' first offline gathering.

Absolutely looking forward to it! I'll keep my sense of humor and make this experience as fun as our gaming sessions. Alright then, I'll go ahead and send the form to everyone for feedback. Let's stay in touch! From comforting each other after losing streaks in games, to creating pet influencers, and now planning scripted murder mysteries—our partnership is getting more and more interesting!
